rationale: C09 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It concerns a maritime-industry strike and shares the child's distinctive factual recital, statutory findings, and complete sequence of operative provisions: Title II powers and duties, a section 206 reporting deadline, and continued existence until presidential termination. C15 is exceptionally close in phrasing and structure but concerns steel, while C03 is also a strong maritime predecessor with nearly identical machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: such dispute has resulted in a strike which, in my opinion, affects a substantial part of the maritime industry, an industry engaged in trade, commerce, and transportation among the several States and with foreign nations, and which strike will, if permitted to continue, imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.parent_excerpt: such disputes have resulted in a strike which, in my opinion, affects a substantial part of the maritime industry, an industry engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmission, or communication among the several states and with foreign nations, and which strike will, if permitted to continue, imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reproduces C09's unusually specific maritime-strike finding, including its syntax and sequence, while omitting only some listed forms of interstate activity and C09's additional perishable-products finding.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of such Act on or before June 30, 1961.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before October 10, 1959.
shared_material.explanation: The operative language is essentially verbatim apart from capitalization and the substituted reporting date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Upon the submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.explanation: The continuation-and-termination provision is reproduced almost word for word, completing the same operative sequence.
